newsitem.title: UK: BAA shares drop on tax report.
newsitem.headline: BAA shares drop on tax report.

text.p: Shares in airport operator BAA Plc were lower in pre-trading on Thursday in the wake of a newspaper report suggesting that it could face a huge tax bill under a Labour government.
The Financial Times said that BAA could be forced to pay more than 500 million stg if it was included in the opposition Labour Party's plans for a windfall levy on the privatised utilities.
The figure was based on the FT's own analysis of Labour's public pronouncements on the proposed tax.
Shares in BAA were down 14.5 pence at 494 at 0826 GMT.

But SG Strauss Turnbull (SocGen) analyst Marshall Whiting questioned the basis on which the FT had calculated its windfall tax estimates, and said BAA is not regarded as being a prime target for the levy.

"There is some logic for a windfall tax on electricity and water companies, where many people believe there have been excess profits because regulation was loose. But BAA has been regulated tightly and it is on a much lower yield," he said, adding "I don't see the logic of why they should be hit at all."
